newsitem.title: INDIA: India primary market lacked lustre in 96/97 - PRIME.
newsitem.headline: India primary market lacked lustre in 96/97 - PRIME.

text.p: Indian investors deserted stock markets in 1996/97 (April-March), with eight percent of all issues being oversubscribed compared to 39 percent in the previous year, PRIME said on Thursday.
The country's leading data base on the primary capital market said 62 out of 721 issues were oversubscribed in 1996/97, compared to 532 of 1,385 in 1995/96.
PRIME said in a statement that 95 percent of all issues in 1996/97 attracted fewer than 5,000 investors, compared to 87 percent in the previous year, which it said refleted a "flight of investors".
Of the 14 issues of more than one billion rupees ($280 million) in 1996/97, nine attracted more than 100,000 investors. One private sector company TISCO figured in the list, PRIME said.
In 1994/95, 101 issues drew more than 100,000 investors.
The data base firm said that in 1994/95, a total of 51.1 million applications were received for 1,340 public issues.
The number of applications fell to 7.2 million for 1,385 issues in 1995/96, and to 4.5 million in 1996/97, PRIME said, adding that the figures showed "investors' apathy".
All 412 issues aimed at non-resident Indians in 1996/97 failed, with the number of applications falling to 8,350 from 19,700 in 1995/96..
In 1994/95, non-resident Indians sent in 188,000 applications for Indian public issues. Roughly 20 million poeple of Indian origin live outside India.
